metas.name: Norway - BarrenHighlands
metas.note: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - BergenHydrant
metas.note: You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - BlackPolePlates
metas.note: Small, wide black pole plates, with a single line of letters and digits, can be found in southeastern Norway.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - BlackSnowPoles
metas.note: Black snow poles are most commonly found between Bergen and Trondheim. Editors Note: These poles seem to only be visible in Gen 3 coverage. I scanned every applicable remote road in the area and only found 2 locations where these still are the most recent coverage. You shouldn't exclude this area only because you don't see them!
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Bracken
metas.note: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - BrightMoss
metas.note: Brightly coloured moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - LofotenMountains
metas.note: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Maple
metas.note: Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - NorthCoast
metas.note: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - NorthEast
metas.note: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Oaks
metas.note: Oaks are mainly found in the far south of Norway.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - OsloPolePlates
metas.note: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Pines
metas.note: Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Røros
metas.note: The old mining town of Røros can be recognised by the densely built traditional wooden architecture. Editors Note: This only applies to the central town
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Russian
metas.note: Russian can sometimes be seen alongside Norwegian on signs near the Russian border. It is mostly found on roads E6 and E105 near Kirkenes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - RussianBorder
metas.note:
Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

Editors Note: This once again is a bit outdated. The street has been updated in 2025 and is now neither humid nor very overcast. The only exceptions are some side roads around Svanvik. I included this meta nevertheless because some maps might still be using the Gen3 coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - RustyGuardrails
metas.note: Rusty guardrails are almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Sámi
metas.note:
Bilingual signs with Sámi can be found in several northern areas in Norway. While the Sámi languages are very different from Norwegian, the best way to recognize them are the letters Á, Đ and the use of several vowels in a row, something which is uncommon in Norwegian.

Note that not all signs in these areas will be bilingual.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - SouthCoast
metas.note: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, are mainly found on the south coast.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Spruces
metas.note: Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - StavangerStripes
metas.note: Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - Vast Farmland
metas.note:
Large farmlands are mainly found in three areas, the southeast, the area surrounding Trondheim, and south of Stavanger.

The following clues will explain how to differentiate between the three.

The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.

The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

Similarly to the southeast, the farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. However, the fields look more vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway - WhiteHouses
metas.note: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they’re especially common on the southern coast, where you’ll commonly see entire villages made up of them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Norway Deep Fjords - DeepFjords
metas.note: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: https://www.plonkit.net/.
